| **PROS**    | **CONS**  |
|-------------------|-----------|
| 🟢 Comfortable | 🟡 Temples can get in way of hat band |
| 🟢 Full protection | 🟡 Long-term durability tbd |
| 🟢 Price | 🟡 Optics somewhat distorted |

# Summary
I purchased these sunnies after sitting on an expensive pair at the Northumberland campsite. Tired of losing or breaking expensive sunglasses, I bought these thinking they wouldn't be great because of the low price. So far they're awesome, rivaling much more expensive glasses and with no worries about losing or breaking them. Plus, they come in different colors and are polarised. What more could you ask for? Highly recommended!

The glasses are comfortable right out of the box. While paddling or riding a bike, you notice they cover your face/eyes well, with no giant gaps, thanks to the frame shape. Despite this coverage, they seem to ventilate well, or just as well as glasses that are expensive and advertise sweat venting. The temples are quite large, so they can get in the way of your hat band or helmet. Folks with larger heads may not have this issue, however.

:::{warning} Lens quality
:class: dropdown
One warning: the lens quality may be somewhat sub-par. I started noticing this on a recent paddle to Old Harry, where a distorted line would appear whilst looking at the chalk cliffs, giving you a feeling of vertigo. I also noticed some fatigue after wearing the glasses all day. We'll see how this plays out over time.
:::

# Buyer
Anyone kayaking needs sunnies to protect their eyes.

# Specs
Cost: £25 on amazon [here](https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B0DZ22C4GX?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title&th=1)
